new_decision_rationale: No new decision. This closes a deployment-integrity defect and records the permanent rule the Product Owner set for every future Hotel Admin release.
po_authorization_ref: EXPLICIT Product-Owner authorization, 2026-09-05: 'Treat this as a permanent Hotel Admin deployment-integrity defect and close it end-to-end. The Product Owner explicitly authorizes diagnosis, implementation, CI, merge and deployment of the Hotel Admin/deployment fix to PRE-LIVE .25.'
root_cause: PROVEN BY HASH, not inferred. The live bundle was built with NO NEXT_PUBLIC_PHASE*_ADMIN flags. Next.js substitutes those at BUILD time; absent, it never substitutes at all, so the compiled client keeps a property access on an env shim that is empty in a browser and every capability-gated navigation entry is permanently false. The routes still compiled and still answered by URL, so nothing 404'd, nothing crashed, the unit was active and HTTP was 200 - and the operator lost Internet Packages, Service Plans and PMS Connection. The live layout chunk (layout-215f6b25f54fabaa.js, sha256 4f19fe07...) is byte-identical to a local build of the same source made WITHOUT the flags, and differs from the same source built WITH them (layout-4b937439c4024f66.js, sha256 c3290d66...). Two aggravating conditions were found with it: /opt/stayconnect/hotel-admin was a plain DIRECTORY rather than the verified release symlink, because the 2026-08-31 bundle was installed by copying instead of through the deployment script, which left the live UI with no provenance at all; and hotel-admin.previous still pointed at release 20260826-084348, which predates these surfaces - a rollback that would have deepened the outage while appearing to be recovery. NOT the cause: stale source (the bundle was built from c0207a28, the master of the day), wrong release selection, or an automatic rollback.
why_it_recurred: THIS WAS THE THIRD OCCURRENCE. The same failure followed the T0093 deployment and was corrected operationally in release 20260825-191137, and current_state_facts.hotel_admin_build_flags_required has recorded 'NEXT_PUBLIC_PHASE2_ADMIN=1 NEXT_PUBLIC_PHASE3_ADMIN=1' ever since, with the note ending 'Every Hotel Admin build must set both flags.' The requirement was known, written down, and correct. It recurred because it existed ONLY as that sentence: `npm run build` succeeded quietly without the flags, and no packaging, installation or health check could tell the resulting bundle from a good one.
permanent_rule: hotel-admin/capability-contract.json is now DATA the build is held to. PACKAGING supplies the flags from it, refuses to build an unconstrained UI, refuses a bundle whose source commit cannot be identified, PROVES the substitution actually happened by refusing any residual runtime lookup of a required flag in the client chunks, asserts every required operator route and each named navigation entry, and writes hotel-admin-release.json recording source commit, BUILD_ID, release timestamp, the flags and their values, and the contract version, plus a sha256 beside the tarball. INSTALLATION re-derives the checksum before extracting, re-proves the manifest and the whole contract ON THE APPLIANCE against the artefact that actually arrived, optionally pins the expected commit, and only then switches the symlink; after the switch it SMOKE-TESTS the live endpoint for the served BUILD_ID and for every required operator surface, and a failure restores the previous verified release. ROLLBACK is held to the same contract: an obsolete UI is archive evidence, never an executable rollback, and an ineligible previous pointer - including one inherited from an earlier deployment - is CLEARED. Release selection is explicit and provenance-verified, never by mtime or 'latest-looking' directory. deploy/scripts/check-hotel-admin-integrity.sh re-proves all of it on demand, with five self-test cases reproducing each live condition.
deployment: PRE-LIVE 172.21.60.25 now serves Hotel Admin release 20260905-000420, built from 822e839581e7 (clean) with BUILD_ID IHj6T6xLCvQBkQC4vZvIN and flags NEXT_PUBLIC_PHASE2_ADMIN=1, NEXT_PUBLIC_PHASE3_ADMIN=1; artifact sha256 546a55b1c93c812fbd5671e871c6ef447bbcc09c78993bf25909fecb7782e43c. hotel-admin.previous points at 20260905-000107, the first corrected release, which satisfies the contract and is therefore a legitimate rollback. The unmanaged plain directory that had been live was moved to releases/hotel-admin-archive/unmanaged-20260905-000112: it is preserved as evidence and is reachable by neither pointer, systemd nor Caddy. Release 20260826-084348 remains on disk under normal retention and is no longer wired as a rollback.
live_verification: Through the real URL, with Caddy's own vhost host header: the served document carries BUILD_ID IHj6T6xLCvQBkQC4vZvIN, matching the installed release; all ten required operator surfaces answer 307 to /login, which is the correct unauthenticated response and not the 404 a missing route returns; the layout chunk the browser downloads is byte-identical to the one in the release directory (sha256 f9885c72...); that chunk contains ZERO residual capability-flag lookups; and it carries the navigation entries themselves - {href:"/internet-packages",label:"Internet packages"}, 'Service plans' and 'PMS connection' - which is the thing the operator had lost. The archived old bundle still shows the runtime lookup, and is not servable. check-hotel-admin-integrity.sh reports PASS on all nine checks.
phase4_stays_dark: The first draft of the contract required NEXT_PUBLIC_PHASE4_ADMIN=1 and the Phase-4 DARK gate refused it, correctly: Phase 4 is accepted at DARK maturity with no financial traffic authorized. The contract now requires exactly the two flags governance had already recorded and names PHASE4/5/6 as deliberately unset with the reason. The DARK gate itself was tested against a proxy - it grepped for the flag NAME, so it fired on a line recording the flag as OFF, and the only way to satisfy it was to stop writing down which surfaces are disabled. It now refuses ENABLEMENT (1, true, yes) and was proven to still catch a real one.
ui_identity_separated: current_state_facts.hotel_admin_runtime_identity records the UI's own commit, BUILD_ID, release, artifact checksum and flags, separately from deployed_head_on_appliance, which names the commit that produced the service binaries. A backend deployment that does not rebuild the UI now cannot imply the UI moved with it - which is exactly what let a UI five days older than the backend be reported as current.
